record_args: Create a space-opera photograph centered on a visible encounter at an orbital shipyard. The main figure is a human professional: a clearly adult fictional chief engineer in her thirties. Use the supplied portrait for her visible facial and hair appearance: facial proportions, dark eyes, and a short dark bob with wispy fringe. Her role, circumstances, clothing, and bearing belong to this fictional scene. A relief freighter is about to leave a ring-shaped construction berth above a pale blue planet. On a narrow pressurized inspection gallery, the engineer is handing the incoming captain a battered rectangular control cassette, the size of a paperback book. Her right hand supports its near edge from below; the captain's left palm has already closed around the far edge, creating one clear shared grip before release. Both hands and the whole cassette are visible between their torsos. She keeps her other hand on the waist-high railing, standing securely with her weight over both boots. The captain, a separate adult figure in a dark travelling coat, watches the cassette; she looks up toward his face with a tired, private half-smile as a green test lamp beside the docking window has just come on. Their physical ease suggests that the risky repair is finally finished. The engineer wears a faded ochre utility jacket over a charcoal work shirt, its collar loosely open, with one sleeve pushed back and small grease traces on the cuff. Her short hair catches a warm line of reflected sunlight, and her quiet, assured presence carries subtle everyday attraction. Behind the glass, the immense freighter's patched silver flank fills the middle distance. Curved dock ribs, servicing bridges, and a tiny tug far below establish its scale and its attachment to the orbital yard; the planet's curved horizon remains clearly beyond the structure. A few work lights still burn along the hull seams. One broad servicing bridge visibly meets a closed freighter access port, while two heavier cradle struts meet the ship underside and continue into the dock ring; their separate junctions can be traced in the same view. Use a horizontal environmental portrait at waist height with a moderate wide lens, the two people forming a compact foreground pair on the left and the freighter sweeping away to the right. Preserve enough depth of field to read the cassette, faces, docking supports, and planetary curve together. Cool window light and low amber work lamps shape worn metal, real skin texture, and restrained blue-gray shadows. The image feels like an intimate handover inside an enormous working civilization, photographed at the precise instant that responsibility changes hands.

record_args: A photographic space-opera scene centered on a fictional woman using the supplied portrait for face and hair appearance, a clearly adult professional quartermaster aboard a battered frontier freighter. Her chin-length dark brown bob, wispy separated bangs, soft oval face and brown eyes draw on the reference. In this independently staged moment of consequential activity, she has opened the last insulated medicine case on a waist-high cargo trolley; there are three remaining silver dose cylinders in total, two seated in the molded recesses and one held above an empty matching recess, with many other recesses visibly empty. Her left palm rests on the case rim while her right hand holds the third cylinder above its matching socket, pausing as she measures what remains. Her open work-jacket collar and loose hair catch a warm task light, giving her composed presence a quiet human warmth within the severe machinery. She wears a faded rust-colored utility jacket, charcoal trousers and practical deck boots. Her lips press together and her gaze has shifted from the dwindling stock toward the observation port beside the trolley. Through that large port, the freighter's scuffed docking collar curves across the near edge of the view, a small settlement's illuminated landing beacon glows on the dark moon below, and a long military cruiser hangs farther out across the route to the settlement. The spatial separation between fragile cargo, near hull, inhabited moon and remote warship makes the supplies feel small against a political frontier. Empty cargo tie-down bays lead toward the closed inner freight door, with one frayed manifest sleeve lying flat beneath the case. Frame her from knee height upward in a horizontal environmental portrait, camera at her chest height and three-quarter angle to the case, close enough that her face, both hands, all dose recesses and the window relationship remain legible together. The trolley supports the whole case; both boots are planted on the gridded deck, with her weight resting evenly as she pauses. Cool moonlight defines the worn metal and her hair edge, while the single amber task lamp picks out her face and the remaining cylinders. Expose for her face and the case rim so their midtones remain readable; the moonlit window stays brighter, while the recessed cargo bays hold a distinct lower tone. Restrained film grain, honest skin texture, subdued steel blue and rust, deep but readable shadows, a candid cinematic photograph of an inhabited working ship.

record_args: A cinematic space opera photograph of a spacefaring crew at work aboard a starship. A fictional adult human navigator with a soft oval face, large dark eyes, a straight dark chin-length bob and airy fringe uses the supplied portrait only as face-and-hair appearance guidance. She wears a charcoal wrap-front ship uniform with an ivory collar; her composed concentration and a small private smile give her quiet magnetism. Two alien shipmates flank her at a waist-high navigation table: a tall rust-red crew member with layered coral-like cranial plates, and a compact blue-grey amphibious crew member with smooth skin and a translucent throat frill. Together they calibrate a forty-centimeter brass navigation lens in its open circular cradle, tilted diagonally toward a clear star mark on the far tabletop. The navigator turns the inner ring with her right hand, her left palm steady on the near table edge. The amphibious shipmate grips the outer cradle at the far left, while the plated shipmate adjusts a small side dial at the right; each working hand remains visibly connected to its own forearm. A single narrow amber ray passes through the lens and lands on a star mark on the table, making their shared progress tangible. Their gazes converge on that meeting point. Behind their shoulders, a tall sealed viewport reveals an immense escorted convoy curving past a pale fractured moon, a distant capital ship dwarfing the smaller vessels. The chartroom is worn, warm and inhabited, with repaired panel seams and one faded fleet pennant. Warm practical lamps shape the three faces; cold moonlight separates the silhouettes. A medium-wide three-quarter view from slightly above table height keeps all three faces, hands, lens and ray endpoint readable together, with the convoy providing immense depth. Natural skin and material texture, restrained cinematic color, a candid instant of mutual trust under the pressure of an interstellar voyage.
